task_instance: Attempt to diagnose/fix a 'Browser extension is not connected' conflict between Claude.app's and Claude Code CLI's chrome-native-host processes by following the skill's Quick Diagnosis and Full Reset Procedure (checking NativeMessagingHosts configs, native host processes, and unix sockets, then restarting Chrome via osascript).
blocker_detail: The skill is explicitly macOS-only (it even lists 'Linux or Windows users' under 'When NOT to Use' since it covers macOS-specific paths like ~/Library/Application Support and tools like osascript). This runtime is Linux (uname confirms Linux 6.18.44), with no /Applications or ~/Library directory, no osascript, no Chrome or Chromium browser installed, no Claude.app bundle, and no Claude Code CLI desktop installation directory (~/.local/share/claude/versions, ~/.claude/chrome do not exist). The skill's core deliverable is diagnosing/repairing native-messaging host and Unix-socket conflicts between two real macOS desktop apps (Claude.app/Cowork and Claude Code CLI) both talking to a live Chrome browser extension. None of that stack (macOS OS, Chrome with the Claude extension installed, the Claude.app/Claude Code native-host binaries and their NativeMessagingHosts registrations) exists or can be installed in this Linux devcontainer runtime, so there is nothing real to troubleshoot or verify a fix against.
evidence: Ran `uname -a` -> Linux vm 6.18.44-fc-v37 ... x86_64 GNU/Linux. Checked for macOS-specific paths/tools referenced throughout the skill: `ls ~/Library` -> 'No such file or directory'; `ls /Applications` -> 'No such file or directory'; `command -v osascript` -> not found; `which google-chrome chromium` -> not found; `ls ~/.local/share/claude/versions` -> 'No such file or directory'; `ls ~/.claude/chrome` -> 'No such file or directory'. All of the skill's steps (inspecting NativeMessagingHosts JSON configs under ~/Library/Application Support/Google/Chrome/, killing/restarting chrome-native-host processes, checking Unix domain sockets under $TMPDIR/claude-mcp-browser-bridge-$USER, restarting Chrome via `osascript -e 'quit app "Google Chrome"'`) depend on a macOS environment with Chrome and the real Claude Code/Claude.app installations, none of which are present or installable here.
